messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a small comparative bench this morning: 7B LLM (int4 quant) across two intra-node configs: PCIe-only (dual 4090-like) vs SXM (A100 pool) on the same host. baseline script: `tools/bench/run_infer.sh --model redwood/7b-q --seq 1024 --batch 1 --streams 8`
priya: nice, what metrics did you capture? latency p50/p99 and tokens/sec? :eyes:
alex: p50/p95/p99, tail CPU, and single-request 99th tail. Also kernel selection flags (fused-kernel vs fallback) and whether NVLink p2p enabled.
marco: main takeaway?
alex: SXM + NVLink gives ~2.2x throughput at steady-state for streaming workloads. but interestingly the tail latency for cold-start requests was higher on SXM when the processes migrated across NUMA zones — saw spikes ~180ms vs ~120ms on PCIe.
sara: migration = process/thread scheduling moving the GPU driver context across CPU sockets? did you pin?
alex: i ran three variants: no pin, `numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0`, and explicit thread affinity with hwloc. pinned run removed most of the tail on SXM (p99 down to 95ms) so NUMA matters a lot.
priya: was NVLink causing extra synchronization that made cold path worse?
marco: could be GPU peer-to-peer warmup or kernel queues getting different placement. did you try disabling p2p?
alex: yes — disabling p2p on SXM dropped throughput ~15% but reduced some multi-request stalls. the culprit looked like the kernel path that copies large KV caches over NVLink when multiple streams touch different GPUs.
bench-bot: automated note: perf traces uploaded to https://internal.redwood/bench/1795559999/traces (perf flamegraphs + nvprof).
sara: what about quantization noise/regression? int4 on 7B can introduce small quality diffs — any eval sets?
alex: ran eval on 3 evalsets: summarization, instruction-following, and codegen smoke. int4 had negligible Bleu/ROUGE drops on summarization but codegen hallucination rate up by ~2.5% on the quantized variant on PCIe. interestingly, on SXM the quantized run had slightly better codegen pass rates — probably due to different kernel math ordering.
priya: that's weird but plausible. kernel math reorder + fused kernels change rounding. did you test `--use-fused-kernel=false`?
alex: yup. fused on SXM gave best throughput and slightly better codegen quality. on PCIe fused didn't help as much and sometimes regressed quality.
marco: action items? sounds like we should: 1) add NUMA pinning defaults for SXM clusters, 2) mark P2P fallback/off as config toggle in the runtime, 3) extend eval harness to include codegen regression for quantized models.
sara: +1 to adding a pinning default. we should also add a perf alert if p99 differs by >50% between PCIe and SXM for same model config.
alex: logging: I pushed a small PR with the bench scripts and the NUMA pin recipe: https://git.redwood/infra/bench/pulls/42 — contains exact `numactl` lines and hwloc binding. snippet I used: ```numactl --physcpubind=0-15 --membind=0 ./bin/serve --gpu-mask 0,1```
priya: can you paste the kernel flags used?
alex: flags: `--kernel=fused --kv-cache=on --p2p=auto --streaming=on --quantize=int4` for SXM. for PCIe I switched p2p=off and `--kernel=fallback` for stability.
bench-bot: bench summary: PCIe (p50/p99) 12ms / 120ms, tokens/sec 450. SXM (p50/p99) 6ms / 95ms, tokens/sec 1000. pinned-SXM p99 -> 80ms.
marco: nice. can someone run a quick cross-region replicate? I want to know if the NUMA effects exist in our eu-west region (different BIOS NUMA config).
sara: i'll queue it on eu-west-dedicated and post results. expect run in ~2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alex: thanks — logs + traces are all in the trace link. TL;DR: NVLink and fused kernels improve steady throughput but NUMA pinning is required to avoid cold-tail latency spikes on SXM; PCIe is more stable for cold starts but lower throughput. runtime should expose a NUMA-friendly default for SXM clusters and make p2p explicit. :+1:
priya: agree. also add an eval step for fused-vs-fallback to catch quality regressions on quantized models.
marco: perfect. keep this thread updated when eu-west runs complete.
infra-bot: scheduled job eu-west replicate (job id 1795564001) — will post results to this thread when done.
